bull.t: Rapid revenue growth and recurring mix
bull.b: Rapid year-over-year growth and a recurring revenue contribution above half of total sales indicate increasing commercialization and a more durable revenue base. Software, advertising, and delivery diversification can support utilization and reduce reliance on any single revenue stream as operations scale.

Substantial liquidity combined with very low leverage gives Serve financial flexibility to fund autonomy development, fleet deployment, and market expansion without heavy debt dependence. This capitalization also provides a buffer while the company works toward better utilization and sustainable unit economics.

A broad deployed fleet and expanding hospital presence create a larger operating footprint, more opportunities to gather real-world autonomy data, and multiple commercial use cases. Multi-year hospital extensions add evidence of customer retention and help diversify Serve beyond food delivery.

bear.t: Severe negative margins and ongoing losses
bear.b: Negative gross margin means current delivery economics do not cover the direct cost of generating revenue, while the large net loss shows that scaling has not yet translated into operating leverage. Without substantial efficiency improvement, growth may continue requiring significant external funding.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and funding needs
bear.b: Cash outflows of this magnitude relative to current revenue indicate that Serve remains dependent on its liquidity and future financing capacity while it scales. Persistent burn can constrain investment choices and heighten execution risk if utilization or commercial growth takes longer than expected.

bear.t: Uber reversal and sharply reduced outlook
bear.b: The guidance reduction demonstrates that partner utilization can materially affect Serve's revenue trajectory, while the expected Uber agreement expiration adds longer-term uncertainty. Reallocating fleet capacity to new channels may eventually diversify demand, but creates transition risk over the next several quarters.
